data.cultural_impact: The name Amaranth is derived from the Sanskrit word "Amar," which means "immortal," and "Ranth," which means "bloom." It is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures including the Rigveda, Mahabharata, and Bhagavad Gita. In Hindu culture, Amaranth is linked with the god Shiva, who is believed to have created Amaranth flowers, which never fade or wilt, symbolizing eternal love and devotion. These flowers are used in various religious ceremonies and are considered sacred.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Amaranth lies in its symbolism of immortality and the desire for eternal love and devotion. It represents the longing for a love that transcends time and space and reminds us of the importance of devotion and selfless love in our spiritual journey. The name also encourages us to strive for a state of awareness and consciousness where we can remember and experience the eternal and infinite nature of the universe and our own souls.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amaranth symbolizes eternal love and immortality. Its name derived from Sanskrit 'amara' meaning immortal, and 'anth' indicating 'flowing'. This name carries an everlasting spirit, reminding us of love that transcends time.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit root अमर (amara) meaning immortal and अन्थ (antha) meaning flower
vedic_reference.note: Not directly found in Vedas or Upanishads.

historical_references.reference: The Puranic mythology mentions Amarantha, a sage and a devotee of Lord Vishnu. He was granted the boon of immortality by the god, which is symbolized by the name Amarantha.

Amaranth was also used as a name for a rare and precious gemstone in ancient India. It is believed to have been mined in the Ratnapura region, now known as Sri Lanka, and was highly valued for its red color and durability.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India (circa 3rd century BCE to 3rd century CE)
